# Final Review Votes
**Producer:** agent:claude/claude-opus-4-6

## Summary

Verified all four amendments against the current codebase. The test-fix amendment (fr-2-e223ad05) is based on a false premise — the test already uses full-precision constants and passes. The NaN migration guard (fr-2-58a15061) is redundant since serde_json cannot produce non-finite values from JSON text. The serde alias amendment (fr-2-6889af6d) addresses a real version-skew risk where a newer TUI client would fail against an older API server emitting only legacy field names. The overview labeling amendment (fr-2-eaad5f11) correctly identifies an inconsistency — the overview screen omits 'Est.' prefixes that the chemistry screen already includes.

## Votes

- `fr-2-e223ad05`: Reject
  Verified: the test helper `expected_gh_d` already computes factors from full-precision constants (100.0869 / 40.078 and 100.0869 / 24.305), not hardcoded rounded values as the amendment claims. The test `canonical_helpers_use_net_water_volume` passes. The amendment's premise is factually incorrect — there is no failing test to fix.
- `fr-2-58a15061`: Reject
  The migration operates on `serde_json::Value` parsed from JSON text via `serde_json::from_str()`. JSON (RFC 7159) cannot represent NaN or Infinity, so `serde_json` will never produce non-finite f64 values. Furthermore, `Value::as_f64()` already returns `None` for non-finite values, which is handled as an error. Adding an `is_finite()` guard is dead code — there is no input path that could trigger it.
- `fr-2-6889af6d`: Accept
  Confirmed: TankSnapshot has no `#[serde(alias = ...)]` attributes. While the current API server emits both old and new field names via `insert_legacy_chemistry_fields()`, this only covers new-server-to-new-client. A newer TUI client talking to an older API server (which only emits `tan_mg_l`, `nitrite_mg_l`, etc.) would fail deserialization because the struct only accepts the new names. Adding serde aliases is a cheap, low-risk fix that closes this version-skew gap.
- `fr-2-eaad5f11`: Accept
  Confirmed: overview.rs line 54 renders '7-ion TDS' and 'Cond' without any 'estimated' qualifier, while chemistry.rs lines 56-63 correctly use 'Est. TDS (7-ion)' and 'Est. conductivity (7-ion)'. The underlying fields are `estimated_tds_7_ion_mg_per_l` and `estimated_conductivity_us_cm`. This is a genuine user-facing inconsistency where the overview screen presents estimates as if they were measured values.
